calibrator_report.summary:
I resumed from run 6's notes. The repo pose is still R7 (committed in f1399d6). It passes every gate, but it bends the middle and ring fingers 64 and 49 deg sideways at the knuckle (MCP), and their finger joints bend up to 23 deg out of their hinge plane. That is the kinked-joint class of defect the right-hand verifier rated major.

This run finished the anatomy-constrained fit that had been cut off:
- g3 re-run with a checkpointing wrapper, fit6c.py.
- The middle tip fixed by a compass search (patsearch6).
- The thumb depths re-solved so the thumbnail turns back toward the camera.

The result, candidate A, passes every gate in Blender with hinged fingers:
- IoU 0.9834, contour mean 0.78 / p95 2.0 px, negative-space IoU 0.935.
- Tips 2.24 / 1.41 / 2.24 / 1.0 px.
- MCP sideways bend (abduction) at most 6 deg; finger joints out of their hinge plane at most 0.3 deg.
- Knuckle line 11 deg off the hand's lateral axis (R7: 51 deg).

The cost: to line the back of the hand up with the knuckle row as drawn, it has to face about 17 deg away from the camera. Then palmar flexion brings the PIPs toward the camera, not away from it as D18 says. Inside the middle MCP's joint gate, the middle finger's 3D P1/P2 reaches 1.21 (D18 asks 1.4-1.6; the ring is 1.36).

With thumb_roll_deg kept at 72, the thumbnail also turns from 12 to 26 deg off the camera. Rolling the thumb to 95 (an exception to D20) brings it back to 2 deg.

Which pose goes into the repo depends on D18 and D20, so the repo keeps R7. The final rebuild (R18, with --views) is of R7 and matches the committed output exactly. Both variants of candidate A are ready to copy in and are verified in Blender.

decisionsForUser.question: D18 against hinged fingers: which left-hand pose should go into the repo? D18 asked for the curled middle and ring fingers to flex toward the palm at the MCP, with their PIPs 0.10-0.15 further from the camera, so that 3D P1/P2 is 1.4-1.6. D18 was decided on the 2026-09-22 pose, whose back of the hand (18.6 deg toward the camera) did not agree with its own knuckle row (50 deg off). The drawn knuckle row (index high on the right, pinky low on the left, index nearest the camera) together with hinged fingers makes the back of the hand face about 17 deg away from the camera. Then palmar flexion moves the PIPs toward the camera, not away. Also, the finger's flexion plane almost faces the camera, so 3D P1/P2 is close to the drawn 74:60, and the middle ratio reaches only 1.21 while its hidden MCP stays inside its joint gate. The only way to meet D18's numbers inside the gates is R7's: bending the fingers sideways at the knuckle.
options: A: hinged fingers (candidate A). Every gate passes (IoU 0.983, p95 2.0, tips at most 2.24 px). MCP abduction at most 6 deg, finger joints in their hinge planes, knuckle line 11 deg off. The back of the hand faces 17 deg away from the camera. D18 only in part: middle P1/P2 1.21, ring 1.36; the PIPs are 0.06 / 0.085 further from the camera than on 2026-09-22 but in front of their own MCPs. Ready as poses/s7/candA-roll72 or candA-roll95 (see decision 2).

B: keep R7 (committed). Every gate passes and D18's numbers are met (1.45 / 1.53; PIPs 0.18 / 0.15 behind their MCPs), but through sideways MCP bends of -64 / -49 deg and finger joints up to 23 deg out of their hinge plane. The knuckle line is 51 deg off, and from above the curled fingers hook sideways.

C: hinged fingers with the hidden middle MCP re-read further up, behind the index knuckle (36-60 px from its reading (612,350)). Middle P1/P2 would reach 1.32-1.40 (anatomy-only solve). This needs a change to assets-source/reference/keypoints.json; as the reference stands, the middle_mcp joint gate would fail. Not built.

decisionsForUser.recommendation: A. It is the only option that meets the task's anatomy constraints (hinged joints, knuckles on a plausible arc) and every gate, and it looks right from every side. It keeps D18's substance: flexion at the MCP toward the palm, and P1 longer than P2 in 3D. Its middle ratio is what this drawing's middle finger allows. D18 would be amended to 'palmar flexion in the hinge plane; P1/P2 as the drawing allows (middle 1.2, ring 1.36)'.

decisionsForUser.question: Only if decision 1 is A: may the left thumb_roll_deg change from 72 to 95? D20 keeps the thumbnail settings as set in the pose files unless the silhouette requires a change. Turning the back of the hand also rotates the thumb's frame, because the builder rolls the thumb from the dorsal. So with roll 72 the drawn nail face turns partly edge-on: 25.7 deg from the camera, against 11.6 deg in R7. Roll 95 brings it back to 2.3 deg. D2 identifies the thumb as the digit whose nail faces the viewer.
options: Roll 95 (candA-roll95, R17): the nail faces the viewer as in the reference, 2.3 deg from the camera. Every gate passes (IoU 0.9833, p95 2.0, neg 0.932). The nail's shape, relief and outline stay as step 3 made them; only their frame is turned back to where step 3 had them.
Roll 72 (candA-roll72, R16): D20 exactly as written. The nail is 25.7 deg from the camera and reads partly as a band across the top of the thumb. Every gate passes (IoU 0.9834, p95 2.0, neg 0.935).
